title: SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications with SanDisk at FMS 2026
event_hint: SK hynix and Sandisk release the first open High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) standard specifications through the OCP, announced at FMS 2026 on August 4, 2026.
problem: Expanding AI inference drives a surge in data volumes to process; HBM supplies bandwidth but limited capacity while SSDs supply capacity but not bandwidth, creating a memory wall. HBF is positioned as a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs to resolve bandwidth and capacity scalability at once.
mechanism: Open HBF standard (released via OCP) defining a NAND-based high-bandwidth memory tier between HBM and SSDs; capacity built from 8-high and 16-high NAND die stacks; UCIe industry-standard interconnect to processors; the specification covers connection interfaces and electrical characteristics, reliability and packaging guidelines for the HBF die-stack process, and software I/O guidelines.

evidence.claim: HBF capacity specifications cover up to 512GB based on two stack configurations: 8-high and 16-high NAND dies.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications...' - capacity specifications paragraph

evidence.claim: HBF bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications...' - bandwidth grades paragraph

evidence.claim: HBF adopts UCIe, an industry-standard connection interface, to link HBF technology and processors, laying the groundwork to integrate HBF across processor types including GPUs and CPUs.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications...' - interconnect paragraph

evidence.claim: The specification was disclosed through the Open Compute Project (OCP) about six months after launching the consortium in February, following the initial standardization partnership with Sandisk in August 2025; Google and Tenstorrent currently participate in the HBF consortium.
evidence.value: OCP open standard; consortium launched Feb 2026 (~6 months prior); partners Google, Tenstorrent
evidence.source_locator: Section 'SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications...' - OCP and consortium paragraphs

evaluation_context: Announcement coincides with FMS 2026, Santa Clara Convention Center, August 4-6 2026. This is a specification-level release (standard covers interfaces, electricals, reliability/packaging and software I/O guidelines), not silicon or system benchmarks. HBF is presented via keynote and panel as a key technology to overcome AI-era memory bottlenecks.
limitations: Specification/standards announcement only: no measured system-level bandwidth, no access latency, no P/E endurance, no write amplification, and no power or energy figures appear in the visible evidence. The ~2.5x power-efficiency and ~540x capacity-versus-HBM figures cited in the source summary are not present in this evidence pack. No silicon availability or volume-production date is given.
project_relevance: Highly relevant to the storage_media question of whether HBF is reshaping the AI memory-tier boundary: the first open standard with concrete capacity (up to 512GB) and bandwidth (0.4-3.0TB/s) grades plus UCIe integration establishes an interoperable HBF tier between HBM and SSD, directly targeting bandwidth and capacity scalability for AI inference. Deployable performance and cost/bit remain unproven until device/system measurements exist.
source_notes: Specification-level facts (capacity/bandwidth grades, UCIe, OCP); no device-level performance or endurance measurements appear in the evidence pack.
